correctness.rationale: For positive integer income profile x with n households and total S, direct logs give Theil T=(1/S)log∏x_i^{x_i}+log(n/S), MLD=log(S/n)−(1/n)log∏x_i. Thus signs depend exactly on integers Q=∏x_i^{x_i} and P=∏x_i with opposite direction for MLD. Enumerate all nondecreasing compositions/partitions x of S for 2≤n≤S≤11 and every within-(n,S) pair (408 total). Independent full integer census finds no even weak discrepancy for S≤10 and three strict reversals at S=11: (1,4,6)/(2,2,7), (1,5,5)/(2,2,7), (1,3,3,4)/(2,2,2,5). Independent Q and P products match given integers exactly. No float comparisons used.
risk: Integer positive incomes, common n and S indispensable; any real rescaling destroys an absolute monetary cutoff.

evidence: General inequality-measure theory addresses parameterized entropy and decomposability for all distributions, not minimal exact integer S for one specific pair.

value.rationale: Theil T and mean log deviation are canonical generalized-entropy endpoints with contrasting tail sensitivity. The exact first integer total at which their ordinal judgments conflict identifies a natural resolution boundary, and three-pair complete first layer improves on an arbitrary numerical example. Scope is mathematically finite and motivated, with no claim of absolute monetary universality.
risk: The value is a small exact arithmetic cutoff, not an empirical poverty threshold or new general index property.

limitations: Strictly positive integer incomes and common total S/household count n.
A change of units or real-valued profiles removes absolute S=11 significance.
